title: Continual Harness: Online Adaptation for Self-Improving Foundation Agents
mutable_substrate: The complete agentic harness H=(p,G,K,M): system prompt, callable sub-agents, textual or executable skills, and persistent memory. In the co-learning extension, open-model parameters theta are also updated between 256-step blocks while emulator and harness state persist.
optimization_operator: A same-model LLM Refiner inspects a recent trajectory window every F steps after a warm-up W and applies CRUD edits to each harness component. The optional model loop uses process-reward scoring, Gemini 3.1 Pro relabeling of low-reward windows, and soft SFT; SFT and offline GRPO provide initialization.
feedback_selection: Runtime feedback consists of detected navigation loops, tool-call failures, stalled objectives, missed exploration, exceptions, invocation outcomes, and trajectory history. Co-learning uses a Gemini 3 Flash Preview pairwise PRM weighted 0.4 progress, 0.3 action correctness, 0.2 reasoning quality, and 0.1 format, followed by frontier-teacher relabeling. Harness edits are promoted directly without held-out validation or a canonical release gate.
archive_memory: A persistent memory store is one of four edited components; skills and sub-agents are separately named persistent stores. Bootstrap-frozen and bootstrap-updating runs transfer the terminal harness across episodes. There is no population archive, lineage database, or automatic last-known-good rollback, and most newly written memories are never retrieved.
validation_strategy: At least three seeds per stated frontier condition; milestone efficiency by cumulative button presses on Red and Emerald; 24-hour Emerald API cost versus 31-milestone completion; pathfinding deficit against a pooled-coverage Dijkstra/BFS oracle; invocation, skill-repair, handoff, memory-reuse, and inheritance traces; judge-verified co-learning milestones; and 20 held-out transition diagnostics for open models. Major missing controls are matched continual play without weight updates and isolated component-removal ablations.
adaptation_mode: Online and reset-free within each run: the harness changes mid-episode and updated state affects the next action. Bootstrap variants transfer a harness across reset episodes. Model-weight co-learning is online in sequential 256-step DAgger batches with persistent emulator state, but scoring/relabeling/update occur between batches and require frontier models.
benchmarks: Pokémon Red milestone suite (18 canonical milestones through the third gym; the main progression plot shows an 11-milestone subset through Thunder Badge)
Pokémon Emerald milestone suite (31 canonical milestones through the third gym; the main progression plot shows 9 milestones through Knuckle Badge)
Warp-to-warp obstacle-aware navigation scored against a shortest-path oracle
Historical Gemini Plays Pokémon full runs on Pokémon Blue, Yellow Legacy hard mode, and Crystal
Twenty held-out Red/Emerald transitions for Gemma-4 tool and action-quality diagnostics
principal_results: Gemini 3.1 Pro Continual Harness from scratch reaches 100% of 31 Emerald milestones at a $130 median API cost versus 98% at $215 for the minimalist harness, approximately 40% lower cost.
Pro bootstrap variants reach 96-100% at $110-$140; Flash bootstrap-updating reaches 80% at $42 versus 77% at $30 for its minimalist baseline, with high variance.

Every Flash-Lite Continual Harness variant reaches only 3-13% at comparable or higher cost versus 20% at $11 for the minimalist baseline, demonstrating a capability floor and possible harm from self-refinement.
From-scratch evolved navigation skills reduce an initial near-50% path-cost deficit to single digits early and accumulate hundreds of invocations over 24 hours.

Five plotted Gemma-4 reset-free co-learning runs make judge-verified progress from beginning- and mid-game checkpoints, while an untrained Gemma baseline and parseable Qwen3.5 controls show no progress.
Historical human/agent mixed GPP runs complete Blue, Yellow Legacy hard mode, and Crystal, motivating but not isolating automated refinement.
limitations: Only two closely related instrumented RPGs are used for automated evaluation, and milestone suites stop around the third gym; full-game evidence comes from a different human-in-the-loop methodology.
The local ASCII map is engineered scaffolding, so the starting point is not literally pixels and buttons only.
Refinement cadence F and warm-up W are formalized but not reported as concrete experimental settings.
The co-learning curves conflate continued play, harness edits, teacher relabeling, and model-weight updates; no matched fixed-weight/live-harness control is reported.
The caption reports five advancing runs without the total number of launched jobs, preventing a success-rate estimate.

The main text says Red bootstrap-updating beats from-scratch at every monitored milestone, but Appendix C reports regression below from-scratch and H_min around step 213 when inherited sub-agent use collapses.
The training appendix inconsistently identifies 31B versus 26B SFT as the initial online co-learning policy.
Most component attribution is observational; most written memories and many created skills are never used.
API cost accounting omits development, training, historical human-refinement, and infrastructure costs, and no convergence point is established.
safety_controls: Environment actions are restricted to eight emulator buttons and harness mutation is exposed through a fixed meta-tool API.
Milestone traces, invocation logs, component histories, shortest-path checks, and judge verification provide post hoc auditability.
No dedicated safety, security, adversarial-memory, prompt-injection, permission, evaluator-gaming, rollback, or safe-release evaluation is reported.

The paper documents an autopress sandbox loophole, a schema-invalid command repeated 842 times, and a persistent Red bootstrap regression, all of which show that sandboxing and direct promotion do not guarantee safe or useful edits.

explicit_predecessors.name: PokeAgent Challenge
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Continual Harness adopts its embodied-RPG benchmark, harness factorization, minimalist/expert conditions, and central finding that frontier models stall without domain scaffolding.

explicit_predecessors.name: Gemini Plays Pokémon
explicit_predecessors.relationship: Human-in-the-loop precursor directly automated by this paper
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The method is presented as a formalization and automation of manual and emergent harness refinement observed in the Blue, Yellow Legacy, and Crystal runs.

explicit_predecessors.name: GEPA and episode-level prompt optimization
explicit_predecessors.relationship: Explicit methodological predecessor extended from prompt-only reset evaluation
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The paper contrasts GEPA-style complete-episode prompt rewriting with mid-episode edits to prompt, sub-agents, skills, and memory.

explicit_predecessors.name: Reflexion and Self-Refine
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Related work positions their between-episode reflective text updates against in-place full-harness mutation from partial trajectory windows.

explicit_predecessors.name: Voyager and Claude Plays Pokémon
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Both are cited as agents that create tooling during play; Continual Harness adds scheduled failure diagnosis and coordinated persistent-store editing.

explicit_predecessors.name: Reset-free reinforcement learning
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The method adopts persistent environment state and frames no-reset operation as necessary for long-running embodied, coding, and operations tasks.

explicit_predecessors.name: DAgger, process reward models, GRPO, and STaR
explicit_predecessors.relationship: Explicit optimization components composed in the co-learning loop
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Online collection and teacher relabeling follow DAgger, transition scoring uses a PRM, offline warm-up uses GRPO, and soft self-training is connected to STaR-style methods.

open_questions: How much of the reported co-learning progress remains under equal-budget fixed-weight, fixed-harness, and no-teacher controls?
Can harness candidates be tested on replayed failures and unrelated regressions before live promotion, with automatic rollback to a last-known-good release?
What selection prior makes agents reuse successful inherited skills, sub-agents, and memories rather than author redundant replacements?
Can an open model act as both agent/refiner and teacher without frontier-model supervision, and where is that capability threshold?
How do reset-free and reset-based training compare under matched data, compute, evaluator, and start-state budgets?
Do full-harness edits generalize to coding, browser use, robotics, or operations when generated code and persistent memory have meaningful security consequences?
What concrete refinement frequencies F and warm-up lengths W are robust across tasks, and how should their cost be counted?
Can component-level causal ablations verify whether skills, sub-agents, prompt edits, and memory each improve end-task performance?
